questions.stem: A 40-year-old female presents with a history of recurrent epigastric pain radiating to the back and accompanied by nausea. She has had multiple hospital admissions due to these episodes. Her serum amylase and lipase are elevated during attacks. Imaging has shown no gallstones or common bile duct dilation. There is no history of alcohol abuse, and her recent attack did not have associated jaundice or evidence of cholangitis. Which of the following is least likely to be an indication for performing an Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) in this patient?
